facts.statement: Carinodens is an extinct genus of marine lizards from the Cretaceous period that belongs to the mosasaur family.
facts.quote: Carinodens is an extinct genus of Cretaceous marine lizard belonging to the mosasaur family.

facts.statement: The name Carinodens means "keel teeth" and was established in 1969 as a replacement name for the previously used name Compressidens.
facts.quote: "Carinodens" means "keel teeth" and was named in 1969 as a replacement name for Compressidens, "compressed teeth", which was already in use for a gadilidan scaphopod mollusk.

facts.statement: Carinodens possessed distinctive round, blunt teeth adapted for crushing primitive clams and oysters.
facts.quote: Like its close relative, Carinodens also possesses distinctive round, blunt teeth for crushing primitive clams and oysters.

facts.statement: Carinodens measured between 2 and 2.6 meters in length, making it one of the smallest known mosasaurs.
facts.quote: Carinodens measured about 2 - 2.6 m in length and is one of the smallest known mosasaurs.

facts.statement: Most cranial fossils of Carinodens come from the Netherlands and Belgium, while the only known postcranial material was found in Jordan.
facts.quote: Most of the cranial elements known from the genus have been recovered from deposits in the Netherlands and Belgium, with the only known postcranial material being known from deposits of latest Maastrichtian age in Jordan.

facts.statement: Dental wear evidence strongly suggests that the species C. belgicus ate hard-shelled benthic invertebrates.
facts.quote: Dental wear evidence strongly suggests that C. belgicus ate hard-shelled benthic invertebrates.

facts.statement: The species C. fraasi was first described and illustrated by Louis Dollo in 1913 under the name Globidens fraasi.
facts.quote: Carinodens fraasi was first described and illustrated by Louis Dollo in 1913 as "Globidens fraasi".

facts.statement: Thurmond proposed the name Carinodens in 1969 as a substitute name because Compressidens was already used for a scaphopod mollusk.
facts.quote: With the name Compressidens being preoccupied by a scaphopod mollusk, Thurmond (1969) proposed the substitute name Carinodens.

facts.statement: The primary distinction between the species C. fraasi and C. belgicus is their dentition, with C. fraasi having unicuspid teeth and C. belgicus having tricuspid teeth.
facts.quote: The primary feature distinguishing the two recognised species, C. fraasi and C. belgicus is found in their dentition. The teeth of C. fraasi are unicuspid and the teeth of C. belgicus are tricuspid.

facts.statement: Sharpe et al. (2024) suggested that the holotype of Xenodens could not be distinguished from an earlier developmental stage of Carinodens.
facts.quote: Sharpe et al. (2024) found that the holotype of Xenodens could not differentiate that genus from being an earlier ontogenetic stage of the Carinodens dental morph.

facts.statement: Longrich et al. (2025) argued against synonymizing Xenodens with Carinodens, suggesting that significant differences in the maxilla and dentition make it unlikely that Xenodens is a juvenile Carinodens.
facts.quote: In their rebuttal for the validity of Xenodens, Longrich et al. (2025) performed CT scans and suggested that the maxilla and associated dentition of C. acrodon differ significantly from those of Xenodens, indicating that it would require a major change in the maxilla shape to consider Xenodens as a juvenile Carinodens, and thus the proposed synonymy of both taxa are not likely.

facts.statement: Carinodens lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
